You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To try investing money, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Download a reputable mobile brokerage app (5 minutes)
Step 2. Research the difference between ETFs and individual stocks (2 hours)
Step 3. Execute your first buy order for a diversified index fund (10 minutes)
Step 4. Calculate your monthly disposable income for investing (1 hour)
Step 5. Set up a dedicated high-yield savings account for your emergency fund (3 days)
Step 6. Read a beginner's guide to stock market terminology (3 hours)
Step 7. Set a recurring monthly transfer from your bank to your brokerage (15 minutes)
Step 8. Verify your bank account via micro-deposits (2 days)
Step 9. Compare expense ratios of different S&P 500 index funds (1 hour)
Step 10. Confirm that your investment portfolio matches your long-term goals (30 minutes)
Step 11. Create a secure password and enable two-factor authentication (10 minutes)
Step 12. Learn how to read a basic candlestick price chart (45 minutes)
Step 13. Submit digital copies of your government ID for KYC compliance (20 minutes)
Step 14. Link your primary checking account to the brokerage platform (10 minutes)
Step 15. Review your total portfolio performance after the first month (1 month)
Step 16. Decide on an initial seed amount to deposit (30 minutes)
Step 17. Select a "Growth" or "Conservative" risk profile in the app settings (5 minutes)
Step 18. Consult with a tax professional regarding capital gains (1 hour)
Step 19. Subscribe to a financial news morning briefing (5 minutes)
Step 20. Watch a video tutorial on how to use the trading interface (20 minutes)
Step 21. Enable push notifications for significant market moves (2 minutes)
Step 22. Attend a local seminar on personal finance (4 hours)
Step 23. Place a small "test trade" with a single share (5 minutes)
Step 24. Research the tax advantages of a Roth IRA (1 hour)
Step 25. Calculate your personal risk tolerance score (15 minutes)
Step 26. Write down your "exit strategy" for losing positions (30 minutes)
Step 27. Rebalance your portfolio to maintain your target asset allocation (1 hour)
Step 28. Interview a financial advisor for a second opinion (2 hours)
Step 29. List your short-term and long-term financial liabilities (1 hour)
Step 30. Determine your "investing horizon" in years (20 minutes)
Step 31. Study the historical returns of the stock market over 50 years (2 hours)
Step 32. Read a biography of a successful investor (1 week)
Step 33. Set up an automated dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) (15 minutes)
Step 34. Archive your first month's trade confirmations for tax records (30 minutes)
Step 35. Review the annual report of a company you admire (3 hours)
Step 36. Define your specific financial "Why" for investing (1 hour)
Step 37. Compare market orders versus limit orders (30 minutes)
Step 38. Buy a notebook to log your emotional state during market volatility (10 minutes)
Step 39. Adjust your smartphone's "Screen Time" limits for finance apps (5 minutes)
Step 40. Deposit your first $500 into the brokerage account (3 days)
Step 41. Research socially responsible investing (SRI) options (2 hours)
Step 42. Listen to a podcast episode about market cycles (1 hour)
Step 43. Join an online forum for retail investors (15 minutes)
Step 44. Draft a simple "Investment Policy Statement" for yourself (2 hours)
Step 45. Check the current bid-ask spread on your chosen fund (5 minutes)
Step 46. Take an online course on "Investing 101" (6 hours)
Step 47. Learn about the impact of inflation on cash savings (1 hour)
Step 48. Print out a summary of your year-to-date contributions (10 minutes)
Step 49. Review your debt-to-income ratio (1 hour)
Step 50. Evaluate your employer's 401k matching program (1 hour)
Step 51. Read the "Terms and Conditions" of the brokerage (1 hour)
Step 52. Purchase a subscription to a stock analysis tool (15 minutes)
Step 53. Determine which sector you want to overweight (45 minutes)
Step 54. Calculate the impact of a 1% management fee over 30 years (30 minutes)
Step 55. Finalize your list of "Top 5" assets to watch (1 hour)
Step 56. Set a "Stop Loss" order for a volatile holding (10 minutes)
Step 57. Check if your brokerage offers fractional shares (10 minutes)
Step 58. Practice using a "Paper Trading" simulator (5 days)
Step 59. Research the history of the Federal Reserve (3 hours)
Step 60. Confirm the settlement of your most recent trade (2 days)
Step 61. Check your credit score to ensure financial stability (10 minutes)
Step 62. Discuss your investment plan with your spouse or partner (2 hours)
Step 63. Double-check the ticker symbols before clicking "Buy" (2 minutes)
Step 64. Bookmark the SEC's investor education website (5 minutes)
Step 65. Set a calendar reminder for quarterly portfolio reviews (5 minutes)
Step 66. Learn the difference between "Bull" and "Bear" markets (20 minutes)
Step 67. Verify your mailing address for tax document delivery (5 minutes)
Step 68. List your current monthly expenses in a spreadsheet (2 hours)
Step 69. Download your first monthly account statement (10 minutes)
Step 70. Learn how to calculate "Return on Investment" (ROI) (30 minutes)
Step 71. Compare three different brokerage platforms (3 hours)
Step 72. Analyze the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of a stock (30 minutes)
Step 73. Review the "Frequently Asked Questions" on the broker's site (1 hour)
Step 74. Check the current interest rate on your margin account (15 minutes)
Step 75. Visit a physical branch of a bank to ask about brokerage services (2 hours)
Step 76. Set up an alert for when a stock hits a certain price (5 minutes)
Step 77. Read about the "Wash Sale" rule for taxes (45 minutes)
Step 78. Take a quiz to determine your investment personality (20 minutes)
Step 79. Look up the definition of "Asset Allocation" (15 minutes)
Step 80. Research the benefits of international stock exposure (2 hours)
Step 81. Install a financial news widget on your desktop (10 minutes)
Step 82. Watch a documentary on the 2008 financial crisis (2 hours)
Step 83. Choose between a cash account and a margin account (30 minutes)
Step 84. Subscribe to a reputable financial magazine (15 minutes)
Step 85. Check the minimum balance requirements for the account (10 minutes)
Step 86. Note the "Ex-Dividend" dates for your holdings (30 minutes)
Step 87. Read an article about the dangers of "Day Trading" (30 minutes)
Step 88. Verify the SIPC insurance coverage of your broker (20 minutes)
Step 89. Learn how to use a limit order to control entry price (30 minutes)
Step 90. Set aside a small "fun money" fund for speculative picks (1 hour)
